sections.html:
The Florida cycle is anchored to January 1, the day each county property appraiser fixes just value on every parcel. Exemption applications are due by March 1. A TRIM notice arrives in August, and the real bill follows in November from the tax collector.

Florida tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
January 1Parcels valued at just value
March 1Last day to file for exemptions or special classifications
April 1Business owners file the DR-405 for tangible personal property
AugustTRIM notice (DR-474) goes out
Sept. to Nov.Tentative and final budget and millage hearings
NovemberBills (DR-528) mailed

If you dispute value, you have 25 days from the TRIM notice. If an exemption was denied, you get 30 days from the denial letter.

Pay early and you keep more. The reduction is 4 percent in November and slips a point each month after that, ending at 1 percent in February. March and later bills pay the full amount.

An account with nothing paid on April 1 turns delinquent. By June 1 the collector sells certificates against whatever is still owed, so a late payer can lose control of the timeline fast.

A homestead exemption can remove as much as $50,000 from your assessment, and it comes in two pieces. The first $25,000 applies to every levy, including the school board's. The second piece, up to another $25,000, applies only to assessed value above $50,000 and does not touch school levies. That second amount is adjusted each January 1 by CPI when CPI is positive, and stays put when CPI is negative.

  • Be a permanent resident living in the home on January 1.
  • Turn in Form DR-501 at the appraiser's office by March 1.
  • The exemption ends if you rent the home out, move away or leave Florida.
  • Servicemembers may rent a homestead without losing it.

sections.h2: How the Save Our Homes cap works
sections.html:
In its first year a homestead is assessed at full just value. From then on, assessed value may rise in a year by no more than 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller, and it never goes above just value. The Department of Revenue posts a cap chart, revised January 2026, with the figure for each year.

Other parcels get a looser limit of 10 percent a year. Either limit disappears once ownership changes, and that covers sales and foreclosures along with any other move of legal or beneficial title.

If you buy again in Florida, you may bring your savings with you. The gap between just and assessed value on the old home can reduce the new home's assessment, up to $500,000, provided the new homestead is set up within three years counted from January 1 of the year you left the old one.

DR-501T goes in with your DR-501 by March 1. Newer amendments start with the 2027 roll, so phone the appraiser to confirm today's limits.

sections.h2: Reading your TRIM notice and November bill
sections.html:
Treat the TRIM notice in August as a preview. It lists last year's and this year's values, the millage each taxing body wants, and when each will hold its hearing. The bill that arrives in November reflects what was really levied once those hearings finish.

  • Look at just value, assessed value and taxable value side by side. On a homestead, assessed value can be lower than just value.
  • Make sure your exemption is listed. If not, go to the appraiser before the 30-day window after a denial notice closes.
  • Compare each taxing body's line, such as the county, school board and city, with last year.
  • Count 25 days from the notice if you think the value is wrong.

Before a sale or refinance, ask the tax collector for a payoff figure on your parcel. Discounts shift every month, so the number changes.

sections.h2: Benefits for older owners and servicemembers
sections.html:
Most of these benefits depend on local ordinance, so your county and city decide what you get.

  • Owners 65 and older: a local government can grant up to $50,000 more if your income is under its limit.
  • Older owners with a lasting disability tied to service: a discount that follows the VA rating.
  • Honorably discharged ex-servicemembers rated 10 percent or more: $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Servicemembers deployed away: a proportional exemption by Form DR-501M.

Deferral is its own program. Ask the tax collector about Form DR-570 before the March 31 filing date and which income thresholds apply to your household.

Every taxing body on your bill sets its millage at fall hearings. The tentative budget hearing falls in September or October, and the final one in October or November. State law ties growth in a taxing body's property tax revenue to growth in Florida per capita personal income plus new construction, unless a super-majority, unanimous vote or referendum goes beyond that.

Proposed millage is printed on the TRIM notice, which makes August the time to plan on attending.

To prepay in installments, apply to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year. Whether you can make partial payments before delinquency is the collector's decision.

Ask which version your county runs. Installments and homestead deferral are different programs with different filing dates.

sections.h2: What a delinquent account can lead to
sections.html:
Following April 1, the collector awards a certificate to whoever bids the lowest interest rate, in quarter-point steps. The holder has to wait 2 years from April 1 of the year of issuance before pressing the owner for payment. After that a tax deed application can be filed.

The clerk then holds a public auction. A homestead parcel starts bidding higher than other property, since half of its latest assessed value is added on top of the amounts due. Pay before a certificate exists if you can, since every step after that adds cost.

A seller's bill is a poor guide to yours. Someone who has owned a homestead for years may be assessed far below just value because of the cap, and that gap closes at transfer.

  • What is the parcel's just value compared with its assessed value?
  • Is the current exemption tied to the seller's residence, and will it end at closing?
  • Are any tax certificates outstanding on the parcel?
  • Which taxing bodies levy on this address, and did any propose higher millage?

Both offices answer by phone or at the counter. With those answers in hand, a buyer or heir can budget realistically before an offer goes in or a house changes hands.

sections.h2: Selling with a tax bill pending
sections.html:
Your title company will split the year's taxes between you and the buyer at the table. Get the current balance, along with any certificate, from the collector beforehand. The property appraiser can say what happens to your exemption once you sell.

The buyer's first bill will probably run well above yours. A sale puts the parcel back at just value on the next January 1, and that happens whether the buyer finances or pays cash. If taxes are behind, the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, so ask for the figure in writing.

faqs.q: When does Florida mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: In November, from the county tax collector. The early discount runs 4 percent in November down to 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: Which date makes Florida taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Certificates on unpaid accounts are sold by June 1.

faqs.q: Which form claims a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Form DR-501, filed with the county property appraiser by March 1. You must have made the home your permanent residence by January 1.

faqs.q: What is the annual growth limit on homestead value?
faqs.a: The smaller of 3 percent or the CPI change. The Department of Revenue chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.

faqs.q: How does deferral work for homestead owners?
faqs.a: File DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year. It covers taxes above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.
